title: Days 5–6: fishes, birds, land animals, and humankind; Cap. 27 close
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): plus finally humankind ye most perfect belonging toward all — plus after less perfect species ye more perfect are made — which answers ye third — but these were fittingly produced on ye sixth day out from earth. concerning whose nature plus use philosophers treat more fully plus more subtly in Physics — namely some cattle plus tame, reptiles, others wild plus sylvan — Moses Genesis 1:24-25 teaching constitutes three genera belonging toward them. Concerning ye creation belonging toward brutes. plus it is belonging toward brutes or belonging toward those endowed with reason. XX. Ye work belonging toward ye sixth day is ye production belonging toward all living things belonging toward earth belonging toward three kinds. XIX. plus is called ye art belonging toward God implanted in things leading them toward their ends — this precept is ye institution belonging toward nature which is completed out from power, wisdom, plus love. Let ye waters bring forth ye creeping thing belonging toward living soul plus ye flying thing upon ye earth — God said. wherefore as if critically ye first answers ye fourth, ye second ye fifth, ye third ye sixth. but on ye sixth walking things plus reptiles toward ye adornment belonging toward earth — thus on ye fifth fishes plus birds toward ye adornment belonging toward waters. just as on ye fourth day stars are made toward ye adornment belonging toward heaven. XVIII. Ye work belonging toward ye fifth day is ye production belonging toward fishes plus birds toward ye adornment belonging toward waters plus air.
pass_b_english: XVIII. The work of the fifth day is the production of fishes and birds for the adornment of the waters and the air. For just as on the fourth day stars are made for the adornment of heaven, so on the fifth fishes and birds for the adornment of the waters, and on the sixth walking things and reptiles for the adornment of the earth. Therefore, as if by critical correspondence, the first answers the fourth, the second the fifth, and the third the sixth. God said: Let the waters bring forth the creeping thing of living soul and the flying thing upon the earth. This precept is the institution of nature, completed by power, wisdom, and love, and is called the art of God implanted in things, leading them to their ends.

XIX. The work of the sixth day is the production of all the living things of the earth of three kinds. XX. And it is of brutes or of those endowed with reason. Concerning the creation of brutes Moses in Genesis 1:24–25, teaching, constitutes three genera of them — namely some cattle and tame, reptiles, others wild and sylvan — of whose nature and use philosophers treat more fully and more subtly in Physics. These were fittingly produced on the sixth day from the earth, which answers the third; and after the less perfect species the more perfect are made, and finally humankind, the most perfect of all.
source_text: XVIII. Opus quinti diei est productio piscium et avium ad ornatum aquarum et aeris. Sicut enim quarto die fiunt stellae ad ornatum caeli, ita in quinto pisces et aves ad ornatum aquarum; in sexto vero gressibilia et reptilia ad ornatum terrae. Quapropter quasi critice respondet primus quarto, secundus quinto, tertius sexto. Dixit Deus: Producant aquae reptile animae viventis et volatile super terram. Hoc praeceptum est naturae institutio quae integratur a potestate, sapientia et amore, et dicitur ars Dei rebus indita ducens eas ad suos fines. XIX. Opus sexti diei est productio omnium animantium terrae trium. XX. Estque brutorum aut ratione praeditorum. De brutorum creatione Moses Gen. I.24–25 docens tria eorum genera constituit — alia nempe pecuina et mansueta, reptilia, alia fera et silvestria — de quorum natura et usu philosophi plenius et subtilius exequuntur in Physicis. Convenienter autem haec sunt producta in die sexto e terra, qui respondet tertio, et post imperfectiores species fiunt perfectiores, et tandem homo omnium perfectissimus.
